# Empirical application

Hedonic price regressions read the value of a local amenity off the
cross-section of property values \citep[see][]{rosen1974,bishop2020}, and
regulatory designations are a standard source of exogenous variation in them
\citep[see][]{greenstonegallagher2008}. Air quality is the amenity with the
longest such literature. The regressor of interest is almost always entered
linearly, and we relax that here, on a two-period county panel whose instrument
is discrete because the regulation that generates it is a rule on thresholds.
The section illustrates the estimator of Section 3 and claims nothing beyond the
illustration; what it does not establish is set out in the last subsection
rather than left to be discovered there.

The data are the county panel \citet{chay2005} assembled to measure how the 1970
Clean Air Act Amendments capitalised into property values. The file holds 989
counties. One candidate control, per-capita expenditure on pollution abatement,
is missing in all 989 rows and is dropped as an empty column rather than as item
non-response, which leaves 22 usable controls and not 23; six more are missing
the local-fiscal block, which leaves an analysis sample of $n=983$ (Table S34 of
the supplement).

Write $Y_{ij}$ for the log of county $i$'s median property value in
$j\in\{1970,1980\}$, $X_{ij}$ for its mean concentration of total suspended
particulates in $\mu$g/m$^3$, $W_i$ for its 1975 nonattainment designation, and
$\Delta Z_i$ for an intercept together with $d_Z$ differenced county
characteristics, at $d_Z=5$ throughout. That is the differenced model of
Section 2 term by term: a continuous endogenous scalar entering through
$\vdagger$, a discrete instrument, a differenced control vector, and a county
effect the differencing removes. Descriptive statistics are in Table S35 of the
supplement, where just under a third of the sample is designated, at a mean of
$0.303$. The intercept is not decoration and A4(ii) requires it: read against
A1b(iv), that clause forces $\Delta Z$ to carry exactly one constant coordinate,
which in a differenced equation is the period effect.

The object of economic interest here is $\vdagger$ and not $\theta_\dagger$,
which inverts \cref{thm:rootn}, whose $\sqrt n$ statement is about
$\theta_\dagger$: the structural function is the hedonic price of air quality,
while $\theta_\dagger$ collects coefficients on demographic and fiscal
controls. Which of the two roles carries the question is a property of the
application rather than of the model.

## The instrument

The designation rule fires on either of two triggers: a county is designated if
its annual geometric mean exceeds the standard, or if its second-highest daily
reading does. We read $W$ as the pair of triggers rather than as their
disjunction, which gives a four-valued instrument: $685$ counties trigger
neither, $114$ the bad-day rule alone, $66$ the annual mean alone, and $118$
both, the last three being the cell sizes \cref{tab:app-localise} prints. The
four cells are ordered in baseline particulates and are not ordered in the
decadal change, so they are not a ladder in the regressor. The refinement
discards nothing, since the binary reading is the indicator of the first cell's
complement.

The reason for reading the designation at $\mathsf L=4$ is methodological and
not empirical. Four cells are what the rule says, so the binary indicator is a
coarsening of the datum rather than the datum itself, and under A1 the three
contrasts the four cells generate are further restrictions on the same
$\vdagger$, by \cref{prp:localise}. What the extra cells do not buy should be
said in the same breath: not identification, since a coarsening imposes fewer
restrictions; not testability, which is present already at $\mathsf L=2$; and
not instrument strength, since splitting an instrument creates no variation.
What they buy is the decomposition \cref{prp:localise} describes, in which a
piece far from zero at the common fit is a cell where the four-valued reading
conflicts with $\hat\varphi$.

All three cells exceed their own reference, at $p=0.039$ for the bad-day cell,
$0.006$ for the annual-mean cell and $0.003$ for the joint cell, against a null
that redraws $W$ from the fitted propensity (\cref{tab:app-localise}). The
reading runs one way only, since a small $p$
localises a conflict to that cell while a large one exonerates nothing:
consistency across cells is necessary and not sufficient for A1 by
\cref{prp:localise}(iii). We report the three cells and draw no ordering from
them.

The instrument moves the regressor. Nonattainment lowers the decadal change in
mean particulates by $8.37$ to $9.11\,\mu$g/m$^3$ across the four control sets,
and does so at the $1$ per cent level at every one of them
(\cref{tab:app-firststage}, Panel A). We read that table on the state-clustered
standard error, because designation was made at the level of the Air Quality
Control Region and A0 assumes independent sampling. Clustered, $F$ runs from
$10.6$ with no controls to $13.1$ at the widest set, so the first stage clears
the conventional threshold of ten at every control set, with little room at the
narrowest. Linear instrumental variables
give $-5.519\times10^{-3}$ log points per $\mu$g/m$^3$, which at the 1970 mean
of $66.0\,\mu$g/m$^3$ is an elasticity of $-0.364$, against the $-0.20$ to
$-0.35$ \citet{chay2005} report on this design; it sits just past the more
negative end of that range and reproduces the sign and the order of magnitude
rather than falling inside it.

A4(i) holds in an in-sample fit and binds in the fit the estimator uses. The
multinomial propensity, projected onto the truncation set of \cref{def:hatT} at
$\varepsilon_\varrho=0.01$, has in-sample minimum $\min_l\hat\varrho_l=0.0115$;
over the $29{,}500$ cross-fitted evaluations one estimation run makes, the
projection binds on $0.997$ per cent of them, at a pre-projection minimum of
$4.3\times10^{-5}$, and at the binary coarsening on none
(\cref{tab:app-theta}). Where it binds, A1 holds at $\hat\varrho$ and fails at
the truncated propensity substituted for it, so those evaluations are outside
the assumption; the theory prices that as a bias term rather than excluding it.
The implied covariance clears \eqref{eq:omegafloor} with room, at
$\lambda_{\min}(\hat\Omega)=0.0113$ against $\varepsilon_\varrho/\mathsf
L=0.0025$, so no cells need merging, which matters because merging strengthens
A1b(iii) and gives back the restrictions the refinement was taken for.

The designation in hand is not the designation that was made. Between 1972 and
1978 nonattainment status was assigned at the level of the Air Quality Control
Region, and the county-level variable in this file is an imputation from monitor
readings. \citet{cropper2023} quantify the discrepancy: the estimated reduction
in total suspended particulates attenuates from $10.2$ and $9.1\,\mu$g/m$^{3}$
across their two panels under the official designation to $6.0$ and $7.7$ under
the county-level definition this section adopts. The imputed variable is
admissible here under non-differential misclassification, so that the
probability of a mislabelling does not depend on $\Delta U$ given $\Delta Z$.
Under it $W$ remains valid and is merely less relevant; under the alternative
the estimator is inconsistent rather than imprecise, so no sample size repairs
it. We assume the condition and do not test it.

## The estimator on this panel

One property of the estimator changed between the diagnostics above and the
estimates below, and it is a hypothesis the theory consumes rather than a tuning
choice. The $x$-direction kernel is the supplement's boundary family at $p_K=8$,
which enforces every truncated moment \eqref{eq:truncmom} asks for, and with it
the clause $\int_{\mathcal X}\hat\nu\,dx=0$ that places the adjoint's range
inside $\mathcal V$. The engine it replaces satisfied neither (Table S47 of the
supplement).

\Cref{tab:app-theta} reports $\hat\theta$ at the headline control set, at
$\mathsf L=4$ and at the binary coarsening, on one cross-fitting stream and at a
common truncation level and iteration cap, so the two columns vary the
cardinality alone. The two agree on sign and on order of magnitude at every
coordinate, and we put the agreement no more strongly than that: measured in
units of the four-cell column's own clustered standard error, no coordinate
moves by as much as $0.53$ of a standard error and four of the six move by less
than a quarter of one. That is the expected direction of no effect rather than a null
result: under A1 the surplus contrasts are further restrictions on the same
$\vdagger$, so they buy localisation and not a different answer, and a large
shift would have been evidence against A1 or against the binary estimate. They
do not buy precision either, the clustered standard error being larger in the
four-cell column at per capita income.

Holding the cap fixed across the two columns is what makes them a one-factor
contrast, and that is not a second-order detail: a third arm at the $\bar m=15$
the binary cardinality would itself have set moves that column further than the
cardinality moves it, by $0.1930$ at its largest coordinate, and the two
contrasts are opposite in sign at five of the six coordinates, so a design that
varied both at once would net them against each other (Table S39 of the
supplement).

The standard errors in both columns are conditional on a hypothesis the
estimator does not impose. \Cref{cor:centarity} makes N1 a condition on a
$p\times(\mathsf L-1)$ matrix, hence $p(\mathsf L-1)$ scalar conditions rather
than $p$, and the anchor this estimator removes is a constant per $(j,l)$ rather
than a function of $\Delta Z$, so it imposes no version of N1 beyond the
unconditional one. What the supplement measures is the smallest defect any
constant anchor can reach, and at $\mathsf L=4$ it is not resolvable from zero,
as it is not at either binary arm (Table S41 of the supplement). That is not
evidence of absence but a statement about the power of the check at $n=983$, and
no moment-level diagnostic could have substituted for it, since
$E[\widetilde W_l\hat L_{jl}\mid\Delta Z]=0$ holds automatically under A1
whatever the anchor is. Inference here is conditional on N1, and by
\cref{prp:orthog}(iii) its failure would cost the propensity direction of the
orthogonality, at the full rate $r_n$ and undamped.

\Cref{fig:app-phi} draws $\hat\varphi$ at the headline control set. The curve
drawn is the four-cell fit, and the binary-coarsening curve does not sit on top
of it: at the common cap the sup gap between the two is $0.0327$, or $85$ per
cent of the four-cell curve's own range of $0.0383$, against a root-mean-square
gap of $0.0136$, so the two separate at some points of the support and not on
average. Letting the cap move with the
cardinality instead would put that sup gap at $0.0081$ and license the sentence
that the two cardinalities agree. That number measures nothing: it nets two
effects that nearly cancel, the cap alone moving the binary curve by $0.0380$.

The curve is not monotone, and the sign the hedonic reading asks for is
delivered on part of the support and not on the rest. It rises at $32$ of its
$59$ grid steps and falls at $27$, in four monotone stretches: it descends to
$-0.0174$ at $48.7\,\mu$g/m$^3$, the 28th percentile; climbs to $+0.0150$ at
$68.5$, the 71st; falls to $+0.0001$ at $86.4$, the 89th; and rises again over
the last four steps. Its whole range is $0.0349$, and its largest sustained
movement, at $+1.64\times10^{-3}$ log points per $\mu$g/m$^3$ between the trough
and the peak, runs the wrong way for the hedonic reading.

The linear slope of the preceding subsection delivers $0.380$ log points over
the $68.8\,\mu$g/m$^3$ separating the 5th and the 95th percentiles of $X$, and
the nonparametric estimate's whole range is under a tenth of that. It is nowhere
as steep either: its steepest single descending step is $-3.28\times10^{-3}$, or
$59.5$ per cent of the linear slope. *The two estimates therefore disagree about
the level of the gradient and not only about its shape.* Every sentence of this
reading is a statement about the point estimate: the constant slope is not a
feature of $\hat\varphi$ anywhere on the support, and the sign it imposes fails
on the two rising stretches, which carry $48.8$ per cent of the pooled
distribution of $X$ between them. We do not call that a negative result, because
the envelope of the next subsection is wide enough that nothing here rules a
constant slope out.

## The bootstrap

Valid uniform inference on $\hat\varphi$ does not exist in this model, and the
obstruction is a property of the estimator rather than of this application.
Uniform bands for ill-posed problems are built on a source condition written in
the spectral calculus of $T^\ast T$ and on completeness of the instrument, and
neither is available here: the operator equation of Section 2 is nonlinear in
$\varphi$, so there is no adjoint in which to write the condition, and a $W$
with four values delivers completeness no more than a two-valued one does
\citep[see][]{severini2006,babiiflorens2025}. Pointwise sets do exist under
nonlinear ill-posedness \citep[see][]{chen2012b}, but they are indexed by a
sieve dimension where the regularisation index of \cref{def:lfstep} is a
Landweber iteration count. We therefore follow the
companion paper \citep{centorrinofeveflorens2019}, which estimates the same
operator equation from a discrete instrument under the same regularisation: a point estimate, a bootstrap band drawn to show variability,
and one sentence saying what the band is not. *The envelope in
\cref{fig:app-phi} illustrates the variability of $\hat\varphi$ and is not a
confidence set. No coverage is claimed for it and none is computed.*

The $99$ replications resample counties with replacement and re-run the
regularisation in each, holding $\hat\theta$ fixed, and the envelope they give
is wide against the curve it surrounds: its median width over the sixty-point
grid is $1.33$ times everything the curve does. Three further schemes ask
whether that width is an artefact of the resampling or a property of the
estimator, since a resample of $n$ counties leaves roughly $37$ per cent of the
draw as duplicates while halving the information: $\mathrm{Exp}(1)$ multiplier
weights, which have the same first two moments and the same effective sample
size but duplicate nothing, and subsamples of $621$ and of $492$ distinct
counties. *That comparison is not evaluable, and we report it as such*: the
three criteria that would have separated the two mechanisms are all statements
about the realised stopping index, and that index equals the cap in every
replication of every scheme, because the discrepancy rule of Section 3 is run at
$\tau_{\mathrm{DP}}=0$ here and the patience is set equal to the cap. What the
schemes do show is agreement on the size of the band, the multiplier arm being
$8.1$ per cent narrower over the grid as a whole and wider at the ends of the
support. The five schemes are set out in Table S44 of the supplement, the
multiplier envelope in Table S45 of the supplement, and the eleven levels this
figure draws, together with the bootstrap's convergence record, in Table S43 of
the supplement.

## What the illustration shows

The estimator runs on this panel and returns the two objects it is built to
return: a slope vector with a clustered standard error, at either cardinality of
the instrument, and a structural curve whose shape contradicts the constant
slope the linear specification imposes. That is the whole of what the section
claims.

At $n=983$ it claims nothing about the asymptotics, and there are two reasons
for that rather than one. Evaluated at $(\mu,r)=(2,\tfrac83)$, the
frontier-clearing configuration the Monte Carlo names, the frontier
\eqref{eq:frontier} is met at no control set that also satisfies A4(ii): it
fails once any control is entered, and the one rung at which it holds is the
intercept-only rung, which A4(ii) excludes because at $\alpha=\tfrac12$ the
sieve-entropy condition admits no integer sieve dimension (Table S49 of the
supplement). The second is
the cardinality arm of the Monte Carlo, which finds the limit law's own
remainder failing to vanish at $\mathsf L=4$ on the paper's named design (Table
S22 of the supplement), in a propensity direction whose price this panel cannot
bound because the N1 defect above is not resolvable from zero. The object that
describes this estimator at this sample size is therefore \cref{cor:ratefloor}
and not \cref{thm:rootn}. *The application illustrates the procedure on a design
the method was built for; it does not demonstrate that the asymptotics bind at
this sample size*, and we would rather say so than let the section be read as
though they did.
